fullPassage: Nearly 200 years ago, Charles Darwin described the first time that he observed ocean water full of tiny bioluminescent organisms. He wrote that the sea was glowing with flickers of light. He also noted that the water still flashed with sparks of light after it was collected in a bottle. At the time, no one knew what caused the glow, but bioluminescence has been the subject of much research since then. Bioluminescence simply means light made by living things. Fireflies are a common example, but the phenomenon is found in some fish, mushrooms, bacteria, and other creatures as well. We now know that the light is made by chemicals called luciferins. The organisms light up when enzymes called luciferases interact with luciferin, and the varieties of luciferin in different creatures produce different colors of light. Humans have occasionally made use of bioluminescence in the past. Glowing fungus growing on wood may have been used to mark trails through forests and miners have used jars of fireflies to light their work underground. Unlike common light sources, bioluminescence produces almost no heat, so it is an attractive tool under many circumstances. Today, even more applications of bioluminescence are possible. For example, it is used to warn of toxic substances in water. Bioluminescent bacteria in water grow dimmer when toxic substances are present, alerting people to test for contamination from pesticides or heavy metals. In addition, inventors are trying to create eco-friendly lamps from algae that glow when the water they live in moves. These lamps are expected to reduce energy usage and light pollution. In medical research, firefly luciferase is mixed with a dye that causes it to emit near-infrared light, which can be detected through relatively thick layers of tissue. This mixture is used to mark blood clotting proteins, making it easier to monitor the effectiveness of blood thinners. Bioluminescence is older than the human species, but modern technology is giving it brand new uses. What was once a mysterious phenomenon is now helping us understand more about our bodies and the world around us, and hopefully allowing us to find ways to generate light with minimal environmental impact.

② glass: 유리 — 몸속 혈액 단백질 표시 맥락과 안 맞아요

③ metal: 금속 — 생체 맥락과 무관해요

④ water: 물 — 두꺼운 층을 통과하는 신체 맥락과 달라요
det.tip: detected through thick layers of ______, mark blood proteins → 조직(tissue).

questions.passage: Nearly 200 years ago, Charles Darwin described the first time that he observed ocean water full of tiny bioluminescent organisms. He wrote that the sea was glowing with flickers of light. He also noted that the water still flashed with sparks of light after it was collected in a bottle. At the time, no one knew what caused the glow, but bioluminescence has been the subject of much research since then. Bioluminescence simply means light made by living things. Fireflies are a common example, but the phenomenon is found in some fish, mushrooms, bacteria, and other creatures as well. We now know that the light is made by chemicals called luciferins. The organisms light up when enzymes called luciferases interact with luciferin, and the varieties of luciferin in different creatures produce different colors of light. Humans have occasionally made use of bioluminescence in the past. Glowing fungus growing on wood may have been used to mark trails through forests and miners have used jars of fireflies to light their work underground. Unlike common light sources, bioluminescence produces almost no heat, so it is an attractive tool under many circumstances. Today, even more applications of bioluminescence are possible. For example, it is used to warn of toxic substances in water. Bioluminescent bacteria in water grow dimmer when toxic substances are present, alerting people to test for contamination from pesticides or heavy metals. In addition, inventors are trying to create eco-friendly lamps from algae that glow when the water they live in moves. These lamps are expected to reduce energy usage and light pollution. In medical research, firefly luciferase is mixed with a dye that causes it to emit near-infrared light, which can be detected through relatively thick layers of tissue. This mixture is used to mark blood clotting proteins, making it easier to monitor the effectiveness of blood thinners. Bioluminescence is older than the human species, but modern technology is giving it brand new uses. What was once a <u>mysterious</u> phenomenon is now helping us understand more about our bodies and the world around us, and hopefully allowing us to find ways to generate light with minimal environmental impact.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 mysterious와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: mysterious=신비로운, 수수께끼 같은 / obvious=분명한 / puzzling=아리송한 / modern=현대의 / tiny=아주 작은

① obvious: 분명한 — mysterious와 반대예요

③ modern: 현대의 — 시대라 의미가 달라요

④ tiny: 아주 작은 — 크기라 의미가 달라요
det.tip: a mysterious phenomenon = 수수께끼 같은 현상 → puzzling.

det.korean: detected=감지된 / hidden=숨겨진 / ignored=무시된 / sensed=감지된 / produced=생산된

det.analysis:

② rare: 드문 — common(흔한)의 반의어 ←정답

④ simple: 단순한 — 복잡함과의 축이라 의미가 달라요
det.tip: a common example ↔ rare(드문).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 minimal와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: minimal=최소의 / maximum=최대의 / slight=약간의 / tiny=아주 작은 / equal=동등한
det.analysis:
① maximum: 최대의 — minimal(최소의)의 반의어 ←정답

② slight: 약간의 — minimal과 비슷한 쪽이라 반의어가 아니에요

③ tiny: 아주 작은 — minimal과 비슷한 뜻이에요

④ equal: 동등한 — 비교라 의미축이 달라요
det.tip: minimal environmental impact ↔ maximum(최대의).

questions.passage:
(A) The old lamp gave off a warm <u>light</u> that softly filled the whole quiet room.

(B) This bag is so <u>light</u> that I can easily carry it with just one hand.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 light의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: light: (A) 빛(명사) (B) 가벼운(형용사)
det.analysis:
① (A) 빛 (B) 밝은: (B)는 무게가 '가벼운'이라 달라요

② (A) 가벼운 (B) 빛: (A)는 방을 채운 '빛'이에요

③ (A) 빛 (B) 밝히다: (B)는 가방이 '가벼운'이에요

④ (A) 빛 (B) 가벼운: 방을 채운 '빛' + 한 손으로 들 만큼 '가벼운' ←정답
det.tip: a warm light = 빛 vs a very light bag = 가벼운.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a fact or event in nature or society, especially one that is studied because it is unusual or hard to understand"

det.korean: substance=물질 / creature=생물 / phenomenon=현상 / chemical=화학 물질
det.analysis:
① substance: 물질 — 자연의 사건·현상과 달라요

② creature: 생물 — 살아 있는 존재라 정의와 달라요

③ phenomenon: 현상 — 특이해서 연구되는 자연·사회의 사건 ←정답

④ chemical: 화학 물질 — 물질이라 정의와 달라요
det.tip: an event studied because it is unusual → 현상(phenomenon).

questions.passage: He wrote that the sea was __________ (glow) with flickers of light. He also noted that the water still flashed with sparks of light after it was collected in a bottle.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: glow → glowing: 'was + __________'는 과거진행형이라 -ing 형태로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'the sea was __________'에서 be동사(was) 뒤에는 -ing가 와서 '~하고 있었다'라는 과거진행을 나타내요. 바다가 빛으로 '빛나고 있었다'는 뜻이라 glow를 glowing으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 glow를 glowing으로 써요.
det.tip: was + -ing = ~하고 있었다 (과거진행).

questions.passage: Bioluminescent bacteria in water grow dimmer when toxic substances are present, __________ (alert) people to test for contamination from pesticides or heavy metals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: alert → alerting: 앞 문장 전체를 받아 '~하면서'라는 뜻을 더하는 분사구문이라 -ing로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
콤마 뒤 '__________ people to test ~'는 주절(세균이 흐릿해진다)을 받아 '그 결과 ~에게 알리면서'라는 뜻을 더하는 분사구문이에요. 주어가 능동적으로 '알리는' 것이라 alert를 현재분사 alerting으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 alert를 alerting으로 써요.
det.tip: , + -ing = 분사구문(~하면서/그 결과 ~한다).

det.korean: air quality=대기 질 / light pollution=빛 공해 / water supply=물 공급 / heat loss=열 손실
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 '친환경 램프 ~ These lamps are expected to reduce energy usage and(이 램프들은 에너지 사용과 ~을 줄일 것으로 기대된다)'가 단서예요.

① air quality: 대기 질 — 줄인다는 흐름과 방향이 안 맞아요(질은 높이는 것)

② light pollution: 빛 공해 — 램프가 에너지와 '빛 공해'를 줄여요 ←정답

③ water supply: 물 공급 — 램프와 무관해요

④ heat loss: 열 손실 — 조명 맥락과 안 맞아요
det.tip: eco-friendly lamps reduce energy usage and ______ → 빛 공해(light pollution).
